messages:
sarah_peopleops: Heads-up question from a manager: employee goes on unpaid parental LOA 2026-11-10, returns 2027-02-15. Our plan year ends 2026-12-31. Do they get the FSA carryover for 2027? Also what happens to claims incurred before termination vs after? Need precise language for the manager.

rebecca_benefits: short answer: it depends on two things: (1) plan design (carryover vs grace period) and (2) whether the employee is considered an active participant at plan year enrollment. Our current health FSA offers a carryover up to $610 (company limit) if the participant is still enrolled for the next plan year.

rebecca_benefits: specifics for this case: because the employee is on unpaid LOA during open enrollment, they must still complete the OE election to be eligible. If they do *not* make an election while on LOA, carryover won't apply automatically. We can accept a retro OE election in limited cases but it requires paperwork.

liam_payroll: operational note: payroll contributions stop on unpaid LOA by default. If someone elects to continue FSA contributions during LOA, they need to set up after-tax payroll withholding or arrange pre-tax via voluntary post-pay (rare). Typically people do COBRA for FSA if they terminate or go unpaid and want to continue coverage.

sarah_peopleops: Manager also worried about termination scenarios: if an employee terminates on 2026-12-15, but had claims incurred earlier in Dec submitted in Jan, are they reimbursed?

rebecca_benefits: If termination occurs before the date of the claim, they can only be reimbursed for expenses incurred while they were a participant (incurred date matters). For health FSA, the run-out/reimbursement period still applies for expenses incurred during the coverage period. If they elect COBRA for health FSA, they can continue incurring eligible expenses during COBRA period by paying premiums. For termination vs LOA: LOA does not equal termination; claims while on LOA can be eligible if contributions/coverage continued.

liam_payroll: Practical workflow: encourage employee to submit any outstanding claims now or before a termination/LOA. If they want COBRA for FSA, benefits team sends COBRA packet and payroll coordinates any required payroll stop/start.

tony_finance: For paperwork we need: completed claim forms, receipts, and if COBRA, signed election + payment. For accounting: FSAs are reconciled to payroll deductions each month; a termination before payroll deduction for the last pay period may leave a small balance the company absorbs or seeks recovery for via COBRA election. We'll handle case-by-case but will escalate if >$1k exposure.

rebecca_benefits: Also note dependent care FSA is not COBRA-eligible; unused DC FSA funds at termination are forfeited unless state law says otherwise. So managers should advise people to submit dependent care claims before leaving.

benefits-bot: FSA & COBRA FAQ: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/fsa-cobra-guide. Open enrollment timeline: OE opens 2026-11-01, closes 2026-11-30. Carryover limit details in plan doc. :link:

sarah_peopleops: Perfect, I'll tell the manager: do OE even if on LOA, submit claims now, consider COBRA if they want ongoing FSA coverage, and dependent care claims won't carry. Thanks all.

rebecca_benefits: if you want, DM me the employee case and i can pre-fill the forms and confirm whether we can accept a retro OE election (we sometimes allow it for LOA with proof).
